title: Derivative-imbalance threshold for vectorial Boolean maps
summary: Determine whether the source derivative-imbalance threshold holds for every admissible vectorial Boolean map, which would improve the covering-radius nonlinearity bound.

formal_statement.body: For every source-admissible pair $(n,m)$ and every vectorial Boolean map $F:F_2^n -> F_2^m$, prove or refute $N_B^F > 2^{n-m+2}(2^{n/2}+1)(2^m-1)$, where $N_B^F$ is the derivative-imbalance invariant defined in the source. The source ranges are odd $n$ with $m<n$, or even $n$ with $n/2<m<n$.

scope.domain: Derivative imbalance and nonlinearity of vectorial Boolean functions
assumptions: n is odd with m<n, or n is even with n/2<m<n
N_B^F is the source-defined derivative-imbalance invariant
scope.unresolved_remainder: No later result inspected through 2026-09-08 proves or refutes the strict N_B^F threshold throughout the complete source parameter domain.

provenance.note: The source cites earlier open-problem literature, but the bounded reverse trace did not text-confirm an antecedent with identical quantifiers and threshold.

citations.label: Fu--Feng--Wang--Carlet, On the Derivative Imbalance and Ambiguity of Functions

progress.summary: The TIT source calls the displayed derivative-imbalance inequality a well-known open problem needed to improve the covering-radius bound.
